project: Claims Correspondence Copilot (Harbor Mutual Insurance, fictional)
question: How should the copilot ground each drafted letter in the customer's policy wording and claim documents?
context_facts: Every letter must quote or reflect the correct policy wording; adjusters approve every draft (Compliance constraint).
Policy wording per product is about 60,000 tokens; claim context per letter is about 2,500 tokens.
Volume: 9,000 letters per month, about 12,000 drafting requests including regenerations.
Pilot: each option ran the same 200-letter golden set, graded by the agreed rubric and a citation check.

criteria.label: Answer quality
criteria.why: Rubric pass rate on the 200-letter golden set

criteria.label: Responsiveness
criteria.why: p95 full-draft latency; 10 s is the SLO ceiling

criteria.label: Run cost
criteria.why: Model usage at 12,000 requests/month plus fixed infrastructure

criteria.label: Operational simplicity
criteria.why: Moving parts to run, monitor and patch (index pipelines, vector store, tool servers)

criteria.label: Auditability
criteria.why: Share of drafts whose cited policy clause is correct

criteria.label: Content freshness
criteria.why: Minutes until a policy wording update is reflected in drafts

criteria.label: Data minimization
criteria.why: Additional copies of sensitive data (indexes, embeddings, caches outside the system of record)

options.name: Hybrid RAG + Claude Sonnet 5.5
options.summary: Chunk and index policy wording (BM25 + embeddings), retrieve top-5 chunks per draft, generate with Sonnet.

options.name: Long context + prompt caching (Sonnet 5.5)
options.summary: Load the full policy wording for the claim's product as a cached prefix; append claim context; generate with Sonnet.

options.name: Agentic search (Sonnet 5.5 + document tools)
options.summary: Sonnet searches and reads policy sections through tools over DocVault, about 4 turns per draft.

options.name: Agentic search (Opus 5.5 + document tools)
options.summary: Same as C with Opus 5.5 as the agent: best quality, slowest and most expensive.
